In that case, here's my gym advice in no particular order:

Keep in mind that any gym with a sales team is offering the membership at a premium. They might quote $45/month but you could get it for $25 under certain conditions.

Newly opened gyms will be cheaper while they acquire members and recoup costs. You can also usually negotiate a better deal by "already having a membership" somewhere else.

Take advantage of trial memberships and don't let them pressure you into a commitment out of fear of losing a "great deal." Half the time the company will send you better deals via email to entice you to rejoin as a former member than the gym's manager will offer you unless you really negotiate for it.

Most gyms also have an employee or manager do a tour where they pretty much try to befriend you while feeling out how much to gouge you. It's like buying a car.

The salesperson is also usually a personal trainer employed by the gym, and will offer you a fitness assessment and/or a free training session. They'll later try to pressure you into buying a package of training sessions from them for 50-100 bucks a pop. This, again, is usually a flexible number, and deals pop up pretty frequently. The trainer may not be able to negotiate training prices, but may know of upcoming special offers.

If you're lifting for the first time, having a trainer teach you proper form and best practices can be really helpful. That said, the trainer affiliated with the gym is often going to be more expensive than most freelance trainers, whom are incidentally often not allowed to train at chain gyms.

Good luck!

There are tons of different kinds of pre workout. Most of them have a ton of caffeine, but I've found that it's not crazy noticeable unless you don't drink much caffeine day-to-day. Aside from amping you up, the caffeine improves blood flow. Not sure what you were expecting, but the marketing is usually a little extreme.

C4 is pretty solid. I like one called ENGN. Muscle Pharm Assault is also okay. Try different varieties and figure out what you like. A few of them have ingredients that are supposed to help you get a good "pump" or increase your muscular endurance. If I'm considering a new one, I usually read up on it in bodybuilding.com and look the ingredients up online. Amazon is a great place to buy most of them, especially if you have Prime.

I actually prefer pre-workout without caffeine, because I often gym late and it keeps me awake. Lately, I've been blending my own using supplements from Bulk Supplements (again, on Amazon). It's cheaper and I know exactly what I'm putting in my body, as opposed to relying on a "proprietary blend."

I'm currently taking creatine daily (not really a pre thing but w/e), and I measure out and take beta alanine (endurance at high reps), taurine (generally good for you and eliminates what would be negative long-term side effects of the beta alanine) and citruline maltate (endurance/pump) as a pre-workout. Definitely do research before blending your own cocktail, though.
